steps.decide: Which attributes a shopper compares at a glance in this catalogue, and expose only those
The image ratio and the weight budget for a grid of twelve
What the card shows when stock, price or variant data is unknown
How filtering and sorting announce their effect without moving the shopper's place

rules.statement: Every card in a grid exposes the same comparable attributes in the same order; a grid where price sits in different positions cannot be compared.
One aspect ratio per grid; mixed ratios reflow the page as images decode and break row scanning.
Above-the-fold images load eagerly and the rest lazily with reserved space; no layout shift is accepted for a grid.
A card missing price or stock says so in text; it never shows a placeholder figure that a shopper could mistake for a price.
Filtering announces the new result count through a live region and keeps keyboard focus where it was.

stateMachine.staleResponseRule: a filtered result for an older query never replaces the current grid

motion.reducedMotion: instant elevation change, no information in the shadow

motion.noneReason: navigation is immediate; an animation delays the destination
the restored grid is already at its default state

nothing is being fetched for an unavailable item
a skeleton has no interactive surface yet

sections.intent: Let a shopper compare a set of products by the attributes that decide the purchase.
nicheDifferences: Fashion needs fit and size context; electronics need spec highlights
B2B catalogues need stock and lead time
a11y: Alt text describes the product, not the file
responsive: One column at 390px with the same attribute order
No layout shift as images decode
copy: Price includes currency and tax basis
alternatives: A list view is legitimate for specification comparison
A table is preferable when many numeric attributes matter

references.label: Project convention: comparable attributes in fixed order (T0405c)

acceptance: Zero visible layout shift on image load
failureCases: Stale results after rapid filter changes
Scarcity claim not backed by data
